A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse Expansion and Wasserstein-neuron research despite the changed title and emphasis. Their main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning benchmarks, neuron-distribution analyses, sparsification interventions, expert-count experiments, and layer-level latency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds downstream-task evaluations, training-checkpoint analyses, neuronal controls, and experiments connecting clustering to entanglement measures.

M1.justification: The matched pseudocode and architecture retain PCA/K-means routing, copied dense weights, cluster-specific SparseGPT pruning, and expert selection without retraining. The new diagnostic metrics and experimental interventions do not change the proposed Sparse Expansion procedure. Explicit GPTQ attribution accompanies retained compression results rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2's evaluation centers on Wikitext-2. v3 retains it and adds SQuAD 2.0, TriviaQA-Wiki, GSM8K, MMLU, and BBH capability tests, plus zero-shot transfer evaluations including ARC-e, ARC-c, Lambada, and SciQ (Section 2.3 and Appendix A.3). This substantially broadens the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The principal pruning comparators remain magnitude pruning, Wanda, and SparseGPT; all already appear in v2's plots. v3 adds neuron-selection comparators based on output mean, output variance, and weight magnitude in Figure 3, and a GMM/BIC component-count predictor in Figure 7's comparison with Wasserstein distance.

E3.justification: v3 replaces the cosine-input/L1-output characterization with normalized L2 distances and mapping difficulty, and changes the central neuron-ablation model from Llama-2-7B to Llama-3-8B. New protocols include specified few-shot and zero-shot evaluations, 17 training checkpoints, and fixed-total-sparsity interventions. Figure 9 accounts for routing in its efficiency axes. These additions and revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of performance recovery after targeted neuron expansion, weighted WD/MD reductions, training-time emergence, weight-magnitude confounds, GMM predictors, PCA-based computational frontiers, and expert-count benefits by neuron group. Appendix A.7 tests preserving high-WD neurons at fixed total sparsity and finds deterioration. The earlier quantized-neuron sensitivity experiment in v2 Figure 4 is removed; existing cluster-count and distribution analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: v3 Figure A10 explicitly identifies its shaded spread as group minima and maxima, whereas the corresponding shading in v2 Figure A.5 is unexplained. Standard-error reporting already existed in v2 and continues in v3; its application to additional analyses does not establish a new uncertainty practice. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark and mechanistic results. For example, Table A1 reports Llama-3.2-1B MMLU scores of 28.729 for Sparse Expansion and 25.046 for SparseGPT at 50% sparsity. Figure 1 revises displayed RI values from 1.11/1.53 to 1.18/1.77. Earlier quantization-sweep results are removed, while v2 Tables 1 and 2 retain identical values as v3 Tables A5 and A3. These are additions, removals, and numerical revisions, not an established across-version performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a central formal definition of mapping difficulty: the average ratio of normalized output and input distances, using median-output and maximum-input normalization (Equation 2). Appendix A.8 develops the normalization rationale, replacing v2's qualitative characterization with an explicit mathematical quantity. The Wasserstein definition remains unchanged; Section 3.5's computational bounds are empirical observations, not new proved theorems.

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds Sparse Expansion as an efficient, leading one-shot sparsification approach. v3 redefines its central contribution around measuring neuronal entanglement and using Sparse Expansion as an experimental framework, adding claims involving mapping difficulty and empirical computational bounds. The earlier pruning-performance claims survive, particularly in the appendix, but no longer organize the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking entanglement to superposition, early training dynamics, effective feature counts, and disproportionate pruning despite modest weight magnitudes. It explains why preserving high-WD neurons can fail under a fixed sparsity budget. Section 3.6 also explicitly judges practical deployment unlikely without memory-footprint optimizations, substantially qualifying v2's efficiency emphasis and narrower acknowledgment that end-to-end timing remained future work.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies calibration on a Wikitext-2 training subset and evaluation on its test set, and explicitly identifies GPTQ in the retained compression setup. It removes v2's A100 counts and MI100 hardware disclosure. The code-access information, RAPIDS dependency, 16-cluster default, pseudocode, and RTX3090 latency setup remain.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts substantially toward polysemanticity, special-neuron research, and computational superposition, adding discussion of Bricken, Lecomte, Gurnee, Stolfo, Hänni, and Adler–Shavit. v3 also distinguishes its use of Wasserstein distance from SWAP and WD-based channel pruning. Much of v2's discussion of DejaVu, MoEfication, activation sparsity, and sparse upcycling is removed.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Sparse Expansion and Neuronal Disentanglement' to 'Wasserstein Distances, Neuronal Entanglement, and Sparsity.' The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Neuron analysis now precedes the method, performance becomes a subsection of the experimental framework, and substantial existing material moves into reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: v3 adds capability radar charts, mechanistic scatterplots, training trajectories, and benchmark tables. It redraws input-output plots, merges the retained scaling and sparsity comparisons into Figure 9 with revised efficiency axes, and adds fitted lines to appendix plots. Existing performance and latency tables move to the appendix, while several quantization panels disappear.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v2's relatively qualitative characterization of entanglement and Wikitext-centered validation. Mapping difficulty, measured WD/MD reductions, alternative neuron controls, the negative fixed-sparsity intervention, and downstream-task evaluations make the central hypothesis more explicit and better tested. The memory limitation also improves the qualification of practical claims. Removed hardware details and some quantization results are meaningful but limited costs relative to these gains; the computational-bound evidence remains empirical.
